title: What Two Forecasts Can Do Together — Wolpert & Breiman Stacking, Yao–Vehtari–Simpson–Gelman Leave-One-Out Log-Score Bayesian Model Stacking vs. BMA & Arsenic Well-Switching Predictions in Araihazar, Bangladesh

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: When none of your candidate models is literally 'the true law of nature,' Bayesian Model Averaging eventually puts ~100% weight on one least-wrong model—whereas Yao & Gelman's Bayesian stacking combines complementary forecasts to win out-of-sample log scores.
teenKit.whyItMatters: In environmental health (like predicting which families in Bangladesh switch away from arsenic-contaminated wells), combining distance and education models beats picking a single winner.
keyTakeaways: In the 'M-open' world where the true data-generating process sits outside our candidate list, classic BMA concentrates all posterior weight onto whichever single model has minimum KL divergence.
Yao, Vehtari, Simpson & Gelman (2018) optimize model weights directly to maximize leave-one-out (PSIS-LOO) predictive log-density of the *combined* mixture.
On Araihazar Bangladesh well-switching data, stacking blends non-nested behavioral predictors to outperform any lone specification.

vocab.meaning: The realistic modeling regime where none of the candidate models in your list exactly equals nature's true generating mechanism.
Pareto-Smoothed Importance Sampling Leave-One-Out cross-validation—fast, accurate out-of-sample log-score estimation from one MCMC run.
Choosing simplex weights w_k to maximize sum_i log(sum_k w_k p(y_i | y_{-i}, M_k)).

quiz.question: Why can Bayesian stacking beat Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) as sample size grows when all candidate models are misspecified (M-open)?
options: BMA collapses onto a single least-bad model, whereas stacking finds mixture weights whose combined predictive distribution beats every individual model
Stacking sets all weights to negative numbers
quiz.explanation: BMA scores each model in isolation and asymptotically picks one winner; stacking scores the convex combination directly for out-of-sample prediction.
